headline: Load-generator's synthetic traffic to the storefront (product-catalog, cart, checkout) has been completely dark for over an hour after a ~90min error spike; app itself verified healthy by direct probe. High confidence.
service: load-generator (traffic source) / product-catalog, cart, checkout (affected downstream, but confirmed not actually broken)
severity_reasoning: No confirmed real-user impact: a direct manual GET to the storefront homepage and to a live product page both returned HTTP 200 in <120ms just now, and the second call visibly incremented product-catalog's own GetProduct OK counter by 1 -- proving frontend-proxy, frontend, and product-catalog are all currently healthy and correctly wired end to end. This is NOT a checkout-blocking outage for a real customer. However, it is a real, sustained anomaly: for over an hour, the only traffic source that exercises this sandbox (the load-generator) has produced zero real application requests -- meaning any genuine regression in the app right now would go completely undetected, and there was a real, unexplained ~90-minute error-rate spike on the checkout/product-browsing path immediately before the traffic went dark. That combination (blind spot + an unresolved precursor error spike) earns medium, not low/none, but the verified-healthy app keeps it below high/critical.
hypothesis: The load-generator container restarted around 07:19 UTC (its own request/iteration counters reset at that point). Within 3 minutes (07:22:52 UTC), its `loadGeneratorTraffic` feature flag started evaluating to 0 (flagd currently reports defaultVariant=off for this flag, whose own description is 'Turn off to pause all load-generator scenarios'). From ~07:27 to ~08:57 UTC, frontend's client-side spans show an escalating, fluctuating error rate (25%-100% in several 10-min windows) on calls to ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and CheckoutService/PlaceOrder -- most likely draining/in-flight requests from the restarting load-generator failing at the transport level, since product-catalog and checkout's own application logs show zero errors in that exact window (only successful 'Found products from database' entries), meaning the failures never reached the services' application code. By 09:56 UTC all real traffic to frontend-proxy, frontend, product-catalog, cart, and checkout flatlined completely and has stayed at zero for 60+ minutes, while the load-generator's own VUs (steady at 6) and its unrelated flagd-polling calls (loadGeneratorTraffic evaluation, ~every few hundred ms) kept running the entire time -- i.e. the load-generator process is alive and busy, it has simply stopped driving its scripted user-journey scenario.
disconfirming_checks: Ruled out 'app is actually down': direct curl GET http://10.10.1.141:8080/ returned http_code=200 in 29ms; GET http://10.10.1.141:8080/api/products/0PUK6V6EV0 returned http_code=200 in 118ms and immediately bumped product-catalog's rpc_server_call_duration_seconds_count{rpc_response_status_code="OK"} for GetProduct from 135610 to 135611 -- proves the full path (frontend-proxy -> frontend -> product-catalog) is live and correct right now.

Ruled out 'product-catalog/checkout are internally failing': Loki query {service_name=~"(opentelemetry-demo/)?product-catalog"} |~ "(?i)error|exception|fail|timeout|unavailable" and the same for checkout, both over 2026-08-09T07:20:00Z-09:00:00Z, returned 0 streams / 0 lines -- no internal application errors during the escalation window that would explain the client-observed error spike.

Ruled out 'observability pipeline itself is broken' (which would be a self-blinding false negative, not a real quiet period): frontend's own resource metrics (nodejs_eventloop_utilization_ratio, v8js_memory_heap_used_bytes, v8js_gc_duration_seconds) kept reporting normally, at a healthy/low load, throughout the entire window; otelcol-contrib and load-generator's own telemetry (k6_vus, k6_iterations_total, feature_flag_evaluation_requests_total) never stopped flowing. Only the actual app-request counters went flat -- the pipeline is fine, the traffic itself stopped.

Ruled out 'this is just normal low baseline traffic, not a stop': checked raw counters (not rates) for demo_cart_add_item_latency_seconds_count, demo_cart_get_cart_latency_seconds_count, rpc_server_call_duration_seconds_count{service_name="product-catalog"|"checkout"} at 10-min resolution over 6h -- all three grew steadily (~35-150 per 10min) until ~08:36-09:56, then went bit-for-bit flat (identical value at every subsequent sample) for over an hour, which is a stop, not a slowdown.

Distinguished load-generator's OWN traffic from its housekeeping calls: sum(k6_http_reqs_total{url=~"http://frontend-proxy.*"}) flatlined at 6032 from 09:56 onward (zero growth for 65+ min), while sum(k6_http_reqs_total{url=~"http://flagd.*"}) kept climbing steadily the whole time (7236 -> 15161) -- confirms the load-generator process itself never stopped, only its app-facing scenario did; an earlier naive sum across all k6_http_reqs_total URLs looked like traffic was continuing, and this breakdown corrected that.
